en: Climb to Gora: Grade, Art, and Time to Stop
zh: 登山电车往强罗：坡度、艺术与停留
ja: 登山電車で強羅へ：勾配、アート、立ち止まる時間

p.src: At Ohiradai, the mountain train stops but does not continue in the direction it was facing. The driver and conductor change ends, and the train leaves along the other leg of the track. From behind the platform line, the four guides watch the front of the same train become its rear. This is neither a detour nor an improvised move. The gradient is written into the railway: the direction changes three times before Gora. If Ohiradai is not a planned stop, stay aboard and watch the rails divide. Deyama and Kami-Ohiradai are signal stations; passengers cannot alight there.

caption.zh: 大平台的折返：四位向导留在安全线内，看同一列车沿另一股轨道继续爬坡。画面帮助理解换向，不代替站内标识或轨道图。
caption.ja: 大平台のスイッチバック。四人のガイドは安全線の内側から、同じ電車が別の線路へ折り返して上る様子を見る。向きが変わる仕組みを伝える場面で、構内表示や配線図に代わるものではない。
caption.en: The reversal at Ohiradai: from behind the platform line, the four guides watch the same train continue uphill along the other leg of track. The scene explains the change of direction; it is not a station sign or track plan.

p.src: Horizontal spacing shows station order only; the vertical axis uses published elevations, from about 96 metres at Hakone-Yumoto to 541 metres at Gora. The clearest gain comes between Yumoto, Ohiradai, and Miyanoshita. Kowakidani, Chokoku-no-Mori, and Gora look nearly level by station elevation, but the roads outside are not therefore flat. The operator currently describes the 8.9-kilometre ride as about 40 minutes; no station-to-station time can be calculated from the diagonal. Red numbers mark the three reversals, green marks this chapter's principal stop, and blue marks the change of transport at Gora.

caption.zh: 箱根汤本至强罗的车站海拔示意。横向只表示车站顺序，不表示距离或时间；红色编号是三处折返，绿色是雕刻之森，蓝色是强罗换乘点。
caption.ja: 箱根湯本から強羅までの駅標高図。横方向は駅の順序だけを示し、距離や時間を表さない。赤い番号は三つの折り返し、緑は彫刻の森、青は強羅の乗り換え地点である。
caption.en: Station elevations from Hakone-Yumoto to Gora. Horizontal spacing shows order, not distance or time; red numbers mark the three reversals, green the museum stop, and blue the change of mode at Gora.

p.src: A switchback is easy to understand once it has happened beneath you, but before the line opened in 1919 there was no obvious way to put a railway up this mountain. An early proposal considered rack rail. After studying mountain railways overseas, the final design used ordinary wheel-on-rail adhesion and eased the climb through reversals at Deyama, Ohiradai, and Kami-Ohiradai. Its published maximum grade is 80 per mille, an 80-metre rise over 1,000 horizontal metres, and its minimum curve radius is 30 metres as the track follows the folds of the mountain. These are limits, not a description of every metre.

p.src: There is no side that wins for the whole ride. After a reversal, a window that faced the valley may face the bank, and the front becomes the rear. Instead of disrupting other passengers to change seats, watch three things: when the rails extend behind the train, when the crew changes ends, and when the valley opens between close trees. In a busy carriage, keep luggage within your own space and leave the doors and aisle clear. When travelling together, decide before boarding who will watch for Chokoku-no-Mori. About 40 minutes is brief, but long enough to pass one stop. Check live service and crowd information on the day.

p.src: From Chokoku-no-Mori Station, a walk of about two minutes leaves the compact station behind and opens onto sloping lawns, ridges, and outdoor galleries. The four guides do not begin by chasing famous works. They walk the edge of the grass first, reading the rise of the paths, the position of indoor rooms, and the weather. Art here is not separated from the mountain: cloud shadow, wet grass, distant slopes, and the space between a person and a work change the viewing. Treating the museum as spare time before the next train wastes both the admission and the stop. Give it 90 to 120 minutes, or leave it for another day.

caption.zh: 雕刻之森的草坡、步道与山脊：四位向导先看清场地起伏和天气，再决定室外与室内展区的顺序。画面传达步行尺度，不对应一件特定作品。
caption.ja: 彫刻の森の芝生、園路、稜線。四人のガイドは敷地の起伏と天気を見てから、屋外と屋内の順序を決める。歩く尺度を伝える場面で、特定の作品を示すものではない。
caption.en: Lawns, paths, and ridges at the Open-Air Museum: the four guides read the slope and weather before choosing the order of outdoor and indoor galleries. The scene conveys walking scale and does not depict a specific work.

p.src: As checked on 16 August 2026, the museum opens from 09:00 to 17:00, with last admission at 16:30; an adult same-day ticket is JPY 2,000 and the official online ticket JPY 1,800. Its guide gives 60 to 90 minutes as an approximate overview and 90 to 120 minutes for an unhurried visit including indoor exhibits and breaks. This guide uses the longer range when the museum is the principal stop. Entrance lockers are listed, and wheelchairs and strollers may be borrowed free subject to availability; ask staff about larger bags. Exceptional closure, maintenance, prices, and services can change, so check the day's notice.

p.src: At the museum, decide first between a light snack, a full meal, and food of your own. For a 20- to 30-minute pause, the cafe lists a hot dog, coffee, Odawara mandarin juice, and milk soft-serve. The juice has a nearby origin; the other items are convenient refreshments, not traditional Hakone dishes. For a proper lunch, reserve time for the Open-Air Museum Dining room or the buffet instead of forcing a meal into the few minutes needed to change at Gora. Brought food may be eaten only at designated outdoor benches or inside Log Plaza KI-TO-KI, and rubbish must be carried out. As checked on 17 August 2026, the cafe runs 09:00 to 17:00, last order 16:30. The two restaurants keep different hours and may change for season or group use, so confirm them that day.

caption.zh: 雕刻之森的轻食：小田原蜜柑汁来自附近，热狗与软冰淇淋则是便捷选择。需要正餐时另留时间。
caption.ja: 彫刻の森の軽食。小田原みかんジュースは近隣の味、ホットドッグとソフトクリームは手軽な選択である。昼食には別の時間を置く。
caption.en: A quick museum pause: local Odawara mandarin juice, plus a hot dog and soft-serve for convenience. Allow separate time for lunch.

p.src: Gora is the next station after Chokoku-no-Mori. After spending 90 to 120 minutes at the museum, check service, weather, and lodging times again instead of rushing to the cable car because the morning plan says so. Gora currently connects the mountain train with the cable car and lists lockers and paid temporary luggage storage. Continue towards Sounzan only when the cable car, ropeway, return journey, or lodging shuttle still has real margin. When staying in Gora, deal with the bags at the lodging first; when descending later, set the return here. Removing part of the uphill sightseeing is easier to recover from than losing dinner or a safe journey back.

p.src: At Gora, the part of the climb solved by the mountain train's reversals is complete. The same train does not continue: the cable car takes a more direct slope to Sounzan, where the ropeway route towards Owakudani begins. After a full museum stop, Gora can be the day's endpoint. When weather, service, and lodging plans all allow it, Gora becomes the start of the next ascent. Chapter 4 continues beyond Sounzan and reads Owakudani first as an active volcanic landscape with necessary safety boundaries, not merely as a station on the way to a view of Mount Fuji.
